subject: Genetics
title: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium.

hook.text: If nothing changes—no selection, no drift, no migration—allele frequencies stay constant forever. That's Hardy-Weinberg.

buildup.text: In 1908, mathematician Hardy and physician Weinberg proved this independently. Evolution requires disruption.

discovery.text: The equation p² + 2pq + q² = 1 predicts genotype ratios in an ideal population. It's genetics' null hypothesis.

twist.text: No real population meets all conditions.

climax.text: When you find a population out of equilibrium, something evolutionary is happening: selection, drift, or migration.

punchline.text: The equilibrium never holds. That's why it's useful.

quiz.question: What does Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium describe?
options: Stable allele frequencies when no evolution occurs
